meta.name: Model swap on recorded traffic
meta.question: Does a step-level replay of recorded agent calls (Kitaru's model-swap analyzer) pick replacement models that keep full-run task success?

dataset.source: Four synthetic use cases: bank support tickets (the SwapBench bank set run through tau2-bench, hidden split, simulated customer) and three Haiku Tax environments (invoice extraction, insurance claims triage, KYC document checks) with written policies, unwritten prudence rules and deterministic graders. All data is invented.
dataset.url_note: tau2-bench is the framework used for bank support only. The invoice, claims and KYC environments are published in ../haiku-tax/envs (generated from fixed seeds). The bank support scenarios are a private hidden split and are not published.
dataset.license_note: The three synthetic environments are covered by this repository's license; the bank support set is private.
dataset.dropped_reason: 49 tasks excluded by the grader audit (audit_exclusions.json) as ambiguous hidden rules (the written policy contradicted the hidden rule or nobody could infer it): 9 invoice, 26 claims, 14 KYC; none in bank support. The step-check sample also comes from the kept tasks only.
dataset.split_note: No train/tuning split: nothing was tuned on these tasks. Bank support uses the first 100 scenarios of SwapBench's hidden (test) split; the other use cases use the first 100 generated tasks.

conditions.name: full_run
conditions.description: Each model runs every kept task end to end in the same environment (one run per task), graded deterministically, and paired with Sonnet 5.5 on the same tasks.

conditions.name: step_check
conditions.description: Kitaru's model-swap analyzer samples 250 recorded Sonnet 5.5 model calls per use case, rebuilds each request (conversation so far plus tool schemas) and sends it to every candidate once; it compares the candidate's single next step with Sonnet's recorded step (tool choice, arguments, text), and Jev rules whether disagreeing replies are equivalent. The analyzer then names picks (closest, cheapest, fastest, best open model) using a 'within 10 points of the closest match' rule. The analyzer takes at most 8 candidates per run, so each use case ran in batch A (Sonnet, Opus, Haiku, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.3) and batch B (Sonnet again plus GLM 5.3 Flash, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3.8 27B, MiniMax-M3); GPT-6 models were re-run in batch G through the Responses API. Results were merged (src/analyze.py).

setup.prompt_rewriting_note: No prompt rewriting: candidates got Sonnet's recorded requests unchanged in the step check and the same agent prompt and policy in full runs.
setup.tools_note: Write tools are recorded and graded, never executed (Haiku Tax environments); bank support tools act on tau2's simulated database.
setup.user_simulator: Bank support only: Claude Haiku 5.5 simulates the customer in full runs (its cost is environment cost, not charged to the agent). The step check replays recorded customer turns, so no simulator runs there. The other use cases are single-request tasks.

limits.full_run: 30 steps per task, 8192 output tokens per call (harness/run.py); one run per task
limits.step_check: 250 sampled calls per use case, one attempt per call, max_tokens 4096, 180 s timeout, 3 retries, concurrency 32, spend cap $25 per batch A/B and $10 per batch G, time budget 3600 s (raised from the analyzer's 840 s cap for this offline run)

judges.name: deterministic graders
judges.description: Haiku Tax environments: compare the recorded write actions with gold built by construction. Bank support: tau2 reward under the hidden-rule-adjusted gold. No LLM judge.

judges.name: analyzer compare()
judges.description: Deterministic: same tool names (multiset), then canonicalized arguments (key order, null keys, whitespace and numeric formatting normalized); text replies compared after whitespace and case normalization.

judges.name: Jev (TypeSafe, jev-latest)
judges.description: Rules whether a disagreeing candidate reply is equivalent to Sonnet's recorded reply; rulings are equivalent, different or unsure.

grading.tie_break_note: No tie-break rule. Ties in tool-choice rate were ordered by the analyzer's candidate order when ranking (see limitations).
grading.human_agreement_note: Not measured. No human reviewed step disagreements or Jev's rulings in this study.
grading.self_grading_check: Full runs use no LLM grader. Jev is not a candidate. Claude models wrote the environments and tasks, the recorded traffic is Sonnet 5.5's, and Haiku 5.5 (a candidate) simulates the bank customer, so authorship and simulator bias toward Claude models is possible and was not tested.

metrics.name: accuracy (full-run success)
metrics.definition: correct / n over the kept (audited) tasks; every task the model attempted stays in n, and empty replies, no-tool-use and step-limit endings count as failures.

metrics.name: delta_vs_incumbent
metrics.definition: Paired difference in success vs Sonnet 5.5 on the same tasks: mean of (candidate success - Sonnet success) per task, with a percentile bootstrap 95% CI (2000 resamples over tasks, random seed 0, src/analyze.py).

metrics.name: cost_per_correct_cents
metrics.definition: 100 x sum over the n kept tasks of the agent's token cost at list prices ((input - cached) x input price + cached x cached-input price + output x output price, reasoning tokens billed as output) / number of correct tasks. Excludes the simulated customer and any judge.

metrics.name: mean_tokens_per_case
metrics.definition: Mean of input + output tokens per task (input includes cached tokens; output includes reasoning tokens where the API reports them inside output).

metrics.name: mean_calls_per_case
metrics.definition: Mean model calls (agent steps) per task.

metrics.name: tool_choice_rate
metrics.definition: Among answered sampled calls where Sonnet called a tool, the share where the candidate called the same set of tool names (analyzer `tool_choice_rate`).

metrics.name: args_given_same_tool_rate
metrics.definition: Among calls with the same tool choice, the share with identical canonicalized arguments (same_tool_same_args / (same_tool_same_args + same_tool_different_args)); computed for this export from calls.jsonl.

metrics.name: exact_agreement_rate
metrics.definition: Among all answered sampled calls, the share with the same tool and arguments, or the same normalized text (analyzer `agreement_rate`).

metrics.name: judged_agreement_rate
metrics.definition: Among all answered sampled calls, the share that agree exactly or that Jev ruled equivalent (src/analyze.py `judge_adjusted`).

metrics.name: state_changing_steps
metrics.definition: Sampled calls where Sonnet called a state-changing tool; same_tool_same_args_rate is src/analyze.py `write_exact`.

metrics.name: failure_rate (step check)
metrics.definition: Share of sent calls with a provider failure (rate limit, empty reply, HTTP error); failed calls are left out of every agreement rate.

metrics.name: analyzer comparable
metrics.definition: Candidate failure rate <= 0.2 and tool_choice_rate >= (best tool_choice_rate in the use case, Sonnet's own replay included) - 0.10.

noise.method: Sonnet 5.5 replayed against its own recorded calls (the analyzer's reference) in batch A and again in batch B, on the same 250 calls; full-run differences use a paired bootstrap over tasks.
noise.ci_method: Full runs: percentile bootstrap of the paired per-task difference (src/analyze.py). Step rates: Wilson score 95% interval on the counts, computed for this export.
noise.tie_threshold: holds: delta >= -0.05; analyzer comparable window: 0.10 below the best tool-choice rate

results_note: One entry per use case and model, in the analyzer's candidate order (ties in tool-choice rank are broken by this order). step_check: the analyzer's numbers for that model (detail in replays_and_step_checks); Sonnet's step_check is its replay against its own recording (batch A). analyzer_verdict: comparable = failure rate <= 0.2 and tool-choice rate within 0.10 of the best rate in the use case (Sonnet's own replay included); rank among candidates with failure rate <= 0.2; picked_as = goals for which the analyzer named this model. full_run: Withheld: computed from the Haiku Tax full runs, an internal draft whose results have not been cleared for publication (inference providers have not seen their numbers). See README.md, Results.

per_type.full_run_note: Withheld: computed from the Haiku Tax full runs, an internal draft whose results have not been cleared for publication (inference providers have not seen their numbers). See README.md, Results.

per_type_note: Types are the four use cases. step_check_tool_choice: correct = same tool as Sonnet among answered tool-call steps.

failures.definition: The provider answered HTTP 429 after retries, so the replayed call has no reply and is left out of the agreement rates (it counts in the analyzer's failure rate).
failures.example: HTTP 429 from the provider after three retries.

failures.definition: The candidate returned an empty reply to a replayed call; left out of the agreement rates and counted as a failure.
failures.example: The candidate's reply to a replayed call had neither text nor a tool call.

failures_note: Full-run failure categories are withheld with the full runs.

replays_and_step_checks.note: Kept for completeness, not used in the analysis. Batch A sent GPT-6 models through /chat/completions with reasoning off (Luna) or could not run them (Sol: GPT-6 rejects function tools with reasoning on there). entries.note: pipeline smoke test, 2 sessions; not analyzed

headline_findings.finding: The analyzer's comparable / not-comparable verdict matched the full runs for 35 of 44 candidate-use case pairs; of the 9 misses, 4 were called comparable but lost and 5 were ruled out but held.
As a filter it worked: in every use case at least two of the top three models by tool-choice agreement held full-run success, and in three of four all three did.

In three of four use cases the cheapest candidate that held full-run success was outside the analyzer's top three by tool choice, so a top-three shortlist alone would have missed the cheapest safe swap.
On bank support, tool choice is saturated (0.85 to 0.9917 across candidates), and Sonnet repeats its own exact step only 0.48 of the time.
Step metrics track full-run success only moderately: the mean within-use-case Spearman correlation is 0.5434 for tool choice and 0.6287 for exact agreement, over 11 candidates each.

headline_findings_note: Findings 1, 2, 3 and 5 rest on the withheld full runs and are given as aggregate counts only; they cannot be recomputed from this repository. Finding 4 is recomputed from results/runs/.
limitations: Synthetic tasks in simulated environments with deterministic graders, modeled on real workflows but not taken from production.

Possible authorship and simulator bias toward Claude models: Claude models wrote the environments and tasks, the recorded traffic is Sonnet 5.5's, and Haiku 5.5 (a candidate) simulates the bank customer.

One run per task. Paired 95% intervals on the full-run deltas are wide (about +/-5 to +/-7 points), and 'holds' uses the point estimate, not a non-inferiority test on the interval; some candidates sit at the line.
11 candidates per use case, so the rank correlations are rough.
Each candidate replied once per sampled call (no repeats); 250 of 383 to 876 recorded calls per use case were sampled.
No human reviewed step disagreements; Jev's equivalence rulings were not checked against people.

The recorded traffic for invoice, claims and KYC comes from a fresh Sonnet 5.5 run on Oct 21, not from the baseline full runs it is compared with; bank support recordings are the baseline tau2 runs themselves.

The analyzer accepts at most 8 candidates per run, so each use case ran in two batches with Sonnet as reference in both, plus a third batch for the GPT-6 models; src/analyze.py merged them and recomputed the picks with the analyzer's own _best_for.

Batch A sent GPT-6 models through /chat/completions with reasoning off (Luna) and could not run GPT-6.1 Sol at all; those results are superseded by batch G (Responses API, reasoning on) and kept only under superseded_step_checks.

The verdict rule is the analyzer's at the time of the runs: 'comparable' = within 10 points of the closest match, where the closest match was usually Sonnet's own replay. Later commits changed this (see the Kitaru changes below).
Ties in tool-choice rate decide ranks by candidate order: on bank support DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.3 tie at 0.9667 for third place, and GPT-6 Luna (rank 6) ties with Qwen3.8 27B at 0.9583.

calibration.json's tool_choice_ci uses all answered calls as n, but the tool-choice rate is over calls where Sonnet called a tool (for example 120, not 250, on bank support); this export recomputes Wilson intervals with the right n, so they are wider than calibration.json's.
Rate limits removed 9.2% to 17.2% of GLM 5.3 Flash's step-check calls (HTTP 429), so its rates rest on 207 to 227 answered calls.

Costs use list prices from the harness price table (checked 2026-10-19); the open-model provider's prices are marked unverified there, and its cached input is billed at the full input price. Step-check per-call costs assume the recorded number of steps and do not hit the warm prompt cache that recorded calls did.
The bank support full runs for Qwen3.8 27B and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash were reused from the Oct 15 expert-deciders study (same 100 scenarios, first trial) rather than re-run.

The analyzer ran offline: sessions were built in memory from transcripts instead of fetched from a Kitaru server, and the time budget was raised to 3600 s; everything after session loading was the plugin's code.

Changes made to the analyzer afterward because of this study (kitaru commit e96fa2a): the best mix now works per step, named by what precedes the call (what a router can see), and needs at least min_mix_calls (default 20) answered calls per step; the Compare table shows Wilson 95% intervals; provider error messages are kept; today's cost comes from the reference's replay instead of the cache-warm recording; the docs add a small-samples warning and say a mix is a shortlist to confirm with a full replay. Later commits on the same branch: Responses API support for GPT-6 models (f1b93ee), picks measured against Sonnet's own replay as the bar with no cheapest/fastest pick when nothing is comparable (e81e4d0), finalists no longer cut to a fixed top three, keeping the cheapest candidate and dropping only clear failures (7903d9b), judge order-swap and held-out best-mix checks (60551f6, ca49608), and the report framed as a screen, not a picker (0217140).
The full-run ground truth (Haiku Tax) is withheld, so the calibration counts and correlations in this file cannot be recomputed from this repository.
Bank support step checks ran on traffic from a private hidden split; those rows are published with anonymized task ids and without texts or arguments.
